_about.what_this_is: A second, independent, hand-verified gold set — the only other one in this project besides ARCHEAN's tests/golden_capital_chain.json and the ARCHEAN_GOLD dict in scripts/analyze_routing.py. Built to test whether the signals and rules in archean/route.py, measured and tuned entirely on ARCHEAN and cross-checked against the wider corpus only via the noisy typeRdd label, actually generalise to a company nobody looked at while building the router.
what_this_is_NOT: NOT generated by archean.route.classify() or classify_document() — every verdict here was determined by reading the OCR text directly, before running the router on this company at all.
NOT generated from typeRdd — metadata_label is recorded per item for comparison only, exactly as route.py itself treats it: a separate, non-authoritative dimension, never the source of a verdict.

NOT an answer key for a challenge with an answer key — like ARCHEAN's golden chain, this is a hand-built oracle for regression testing, built with the same discipline: null/omitted fields where the document does not resolve a question, never a guess.
NOT exhaustive. Nine documents were read in full; two (541a, 5423) have no OCR and were not read; one (5424) was found to be a near-duplicate of 541c and was not independently re-derived.
_about.methodology: Selection (Phase 1) used only corpus-structural criteria — document count, OCR coverage, typeRdd presence/absence diversity, typeRdd-capital density, presence of a Constitution tag — computed BEFORE any document body was read, and is reproducible from scripts/analyze_routing.load_all_actes() alone. Every verdict (Phase 3) was determined by reading each document's OCR text directly, using archean.route's line-finding functions (_capital_evidence, _topic_evidence) only as a mechanical locator of candidate lines to inspect, never as the source of a verdict. route.py's actual classify() was run against this company for the first time only after every item below was frozen (see scripts/gold_compare.py and its output for the resulting agreement/disagreement).

excluded_from_candidacy.499979540: HADEAN. Already inspected in detail (documents 9133, 9134, 9139) to validate route.py's date-based recital check in the cross-corpus validation step — not independent. Using it here would let a company that shaped the rule also grade it.
excluded_from_candidacy.480489707: ARCHEAN. The company the router and every prior gold set were built on.

company_selected.denomination: JACQUES BOCKEL SARL (SARL, transformed to SAS in 2017)
company_selected.selection_rationale: Highest structural score among the 18 eligible non-excluded companies (score computed on: >=2 typeRdd-capital documents, >=1 OCR'd document with no typeRdd, an explicit Constitution typeRdd tag, >=70% OCR coverage). 12 total documents, 9 with OCR (75%), 9 with typeRdd present and 2 of those 9 OCR'd documents with typeRdd absent, 3 typeRdd-capital-tagged documents (the highest of any non-ARCHEAN company), one explicit 'Acte sous seing privé — Constitution' tag, and three typeRdd entries that are bare named-party pairs (e.g. 'JACQUES BOCKEL / SCHOTT VERONIQUE') rather than a word like 'cession' or 'donation' — a form the weak typeRdd-label rule in scripts/analyze_routing.py does not recognise as share_transfer at all, making it a genuinely independent test of content-based detection.
company_selected.legal_form_note: SARL (parts sociales), not SAS like ARCHEAN — directly exercises the SAS/SARL vocabulary split documented in DISCOVERY.md 8.5.
company_selected.limitation: No document read here supports a clean, isolated 'authorization not yet exercised' case (an authorised ceiling with no realisation) as ARCHEAN's …7ebf/…7ec8 pair does — every capital operation found in this company's read documents was either genuinely realised or a report/recital, never a standalone unexecuted ceiling. This is recorded as insufficient evidence for that specific question, not forced.

_about.structural_score_note: Reproducible via: sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from analyze_routing import load_all_actes, default_data_root, type_rdd_labels — see DISCOVERY.md 8.8 for the exact scoring table and the 8 next-best candidates it was compared against.
_about.provenance_convention: page = 1-indexed PDF page (matches archean.corpus.Page.number). line_index = position in that page's raw ocr[] array, unfiltered (matches archean.ground.OcrLine.index and archean.route.Evidence.line_index exactly — NOT the filtered index route.py's classify() would report after dropping score==0 lines, since none of the cited lines have score 0).

The cited line is resolution 3 (the cash increase), which uses the exact 'pour le porter de X à Y' template.

Cited here from its occurrence within 5420 (page 18); the identical resolution also occurs in 5426 at page 3 (item bockel-5426-capital), which is the primary, page-verified citation for this same operation — both are kept as separate items because they are separate PDF files a document loader ingests independently, even though the underlying legal fact is one operation.

Each act states 'le cédant cède et transporte... au cessionnaire qui accepte' plus an explicit share count and consideration — the clearest possible OPERATIVE-shaped share_transfer text found anywhere in this gold set. Cited line is act (1)'s operative clause.
items.metadata_label_note: typeRdd DOES name the parties for all three acts ('BOCKEL JACQUES / BOCKEL JEREMY ET DOMENEGHETTY MATHIEU', 'JACQUES BOCKEL / SCHOTT VERONIQUE', 'JACQUES BOCKEL / DOMENEGHETTY MATHIEU') but the weak typeRdd_capital/type_rdd_labels share_transfer rule in scripts/analyze_routing.py looks for the words 'cession' or 'donation' in the decision text and finds neither in these bare name-pair strings, so weak_xfer_label is False. metadata_label above is set to that computed weak label (False), which is itself the finding: typeRdd genuinely documents this transfer, but not in a form the existing weak-label rule recognises. This is a distinct case from ARCHEAN's …ec2 misattribution — here the registry data is not WRONG, it is merely in a shape the automated weak-label reader was not built to parse.

known_findings.severity: real, systematic disagreement — the dominant finding of this gold set, not an edge case
known_findings.description: archean.frenchnum.parse_french_date_parts, called by route.py's recital-date check (_cites_earlier_year), accepts ANY bare 4-digit numeral as a year with no contextual validation beyond a 1000-2999 plausibility range. In this company's documents, share/part counts routinely fall in exactly that range, and every recital-suppression disagreement in this comparison traces to this one root cause, confirmed by direct diagnosis (not inferred from disagreement counts) in three separate places: (1) document 541d, page 3: 'euros par la création de 1766 parts de 75 euros chacune' — '1766' read as year 1766 < 2003, wrongly suppressing the immediately preceding, genuinely OPERATIVE line (page 3 line_index 2, resolution 2 of the AGE) into RECITAL. Document-level verdict for 541d still agrees with gold (OPERATIVE), because resolution 3's independent line survives. (2) Document 5421, page 5: the SAME '1766 parts' phrase (this document also describes the apport) sits one line above a boilerplate Article-8/9 sentence that independently, incorrectly, matches TRANSITION+AMOUNT ('...au titre de l'augmentation de capital de la' + '75 euros' — a second, separate false-positive-shaped TRANSITION_RE match, since 'augmentation de capital de' has no requirement that a number follow 'de'). The 1766-as-year misparse suppresses this boilerplate line into RECITAL, and because route.py's classify() control flow is 'if operative: OPERATIVE; elif suppressed: RECITAL; else: check topic for MENTION' — the mere PRESENCE of any suppressed candidate, even a boilerplate one wrongly matched in the first place, produces a document-level RECITAL verdict that skips the topic-only MENTION check entirely. This changes 5421's document-level verdict from gold's MENTION to router's RECITAL. (3) Documents 5420/5426, page 18/page 3: 'euros par création de 2000 parts nouvelles de 75,00 euros' — '2000' read as year 2000 < 2013, suppressing the SOLE operative line in each file (the 'pour le porter de 150 000 euros à 300 000 euros' resolution) into RECITAL. This changes BOTH documents' document-level verdict from gold's OPERATIVE to router's RECITAL — the most consequential instance, since unlike 541d there is no second independent operative line to fall back on. Not fixed here, per this step's explicit scope: recorded as three reproducible cases for a future step, with the shared root cause stated once rather than presented as three unrelated bugs.
known_findings.reproduction: archean.corpus.load_corpus('.../445070311/actes'); archean.route._capital_evidence(doc, archean.route._read_document_lines(doc)) on 541d, 5421, 5420 and 5426 each show the cited line in 'suppressed', not 'operative'. archean.frenchnum.parse_french_date_parts('...1766 parts...').year == 1766 and parse_french_date_parts('...2000 parts nouvelles...').year == 2000 confirm the parser's own behaviour directly, independent of route.py.

known_findings.description: Document 5421 uses the word 'cession' once, in the sense of a future SALE OF BUSINESS ASSETS ('la cession ultérieure des biens corporels apportés'), not a transfer of company shares. archean.route.TRANSFER_TOPIC includes the bare word 'cession' with no sense disambiguation (deliberately, per DISCOVERY.md 8.5/8.6 — narrowing it further has no cross-corpus measurement behind it). Gold labels this document share_transfer=SILENT on a careful reading; route.py is expected to return MENTION for it. This is not a bug to fix here — it is exactly the kind of imprecision 'cession' was already known to carry (DISCOVERY.md 8.5's boilerplate-FP finding), now confirmed in a second sense of the same ambiguity, not just the statutory-boilerplate sense.

known_findings.severity: confirms an existing finding in a second company
known_findings.description: 5420 and 5426 share numChrono 2049 and are one registry deposit split into two PDF files with overlapping content (a capital-increase AGE, updated statutes, and three cession acts, all present in both files at different page offsets) — the same pattern already documented for ARCHEAN in DISCOVERY.md 4.1 (C8: …ec8/…ec9, …eca/…ecb). This was discovered only after both files' candidate-line counts came out numerically identical during construction (33 topic-capital lines, 65 topic-transfer lines, 1 suppressed line, in both files) and were checked directly rather than assumed to be coincidence.

known_findings.severity: observed, not yet a tested router behaviour
known_findings.description: The Jacques BOCKEL -> Mathieu DOMENEGHETTY cession act (within 5420) is signed 'Fait à Saverne, le 07 août 2007' but was not deposited at the registry until 2013-11-04 — a roughly 6-year gap, an order of magnitude larger than any deposit-vs-decision gap measured in ARCHEAN (18 days to 526 days, DISCOVERY.md 5.4/11.1) or in the capital-recital date check (which only ever needs to distinguish 'this year' from 'an earlier year', not measure a specific gap). Not currently exercised by any route.py logic (the date-based check applies only within _capital_evidence, not to share_transfer's topic detection), so this is recorded as an observed corpus fact, not a demonstrated bug.

Every one of the 9 OCR'd documents read in this company registers at least one capital_amount MENTION-triggering line under route.py's current design (topic phrase present anywhere = MENTION), because either a feuille de présence's routine quorum sentence ('X parts sur Y parts composant le capital social') or a report's contextual mention of 'capital social' is present in all of them. This gold set therefore contains NO capital_amount=SILENT item — a real, reported gap rather than a forced example. Whether a genuinely capital_amount-SILENT document exists ANYWHERE in this company's un-read or OCR-less documents (541a, 5423, 541f — the last of which was structurally scanned but not read) is not established either way.

No document read in this company presents a standalone 'authorised but not (yet) exercised' ceiling, the pattern ARCHEAN's …7ebf/…7ec8 pair tests. Every capital operation found here was either fully realised in the same document or a supporting valuation report for an operation realised shortly after. This question (§4.3 of the task) remains untested by this gold set.

unresolved: Whether archean.frenchnum's bare-4-digit-year acceptance should be scoped more narrowly (e.g. a plausible calendar range, or requiring surrounding date-shaped context) is a route.py/frenchnum design question this step explicitly does not decide.
Whether the 'K€' amount-shorthand gap (541c) matters for any rule that DOES require amount (none currently do, since MENTION was resolved not to require it) is untested.
Whether TRANSFER_TOPIC's bare 'cession' should be scoped to exclude the asset-sale sense is a design question, not answered here.

Whether 541f (the full SARL->SAS transformation deed, structurally scanned for topic presence but not read line-by-line) would have offered a cleaner constitution-adjacent or authorization case was not investigated, given the volume of evidence already gathered from the other 8 documents.
